extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) staff, and parties in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing interim suspension of a practitioner from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25, including notice, opportunity to respond, referral to a hearing officer, and interim relief (e.g., limited recognition, dissociation from customer numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for interim suspension (serious crimes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim suspension may be imposed where evidence shows the practitioner committed serious crimes (e.g., guilty pleas/convictions for felonies such as conspiracy, false statements). The Order cites violations of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.804(b), 11.804(c), or, alternatively, 11.804(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director requested interim suspension predicated on evidence that Respondent committed serious crimes (Respondent pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire, mail, and securities fraud (18 U.S.C. § 371) and two counts of false statements (18 U.S.C. § 1001)). Such criminal adjudications support interim suspension under 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.25 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Notice and Order must be mailed to the practitioner (certified mail used here) and provide an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition of discipline within forty (40) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail (receipt number provided) and delivered; it provided Respondent 40 days to file a response. Proper service and the 40‑day response period are prerequisites to the interim suspension process under § 11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner fails to file a timely response to the Notice and Order, there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.25 and interim suspension is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not file a response to the Notice and Order; the Order expressly determines that, in light of that failure, interim suspension is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension effective immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner is suspended on an interim basis from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non‑patent law before the USPTO effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states the suspension is effective the date of the Final Order and that any subsequent review does not postpone or hold the suspension in abeyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b) (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office for a finite period (here, commencing on the date of the Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the signing date) solely to facilitate compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly tailored and temporary; it is granted only to permit the practitioner to take actions required by § 11.58(b) (e.g., wound up client matters/notification obligations) and expires after 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to hearing officer for formal disciplinary proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint is referred to a hearing officer (here, HUD Office of Hearings and Appeals) for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral initiates formal adjudication; the hearing officer will preside over the proceeding under the applicable rules (e.g., 37 C.F.R. § 11.36 for answers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file written answer within 30 days to hearing officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order, the practitioner must file a written answer to the Complaint with the designated hearing officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides mailing and hand‑delivery addresses for the HUD Docket Clerk and requires a PDF of the answer be filed via email to alj.ali@hud.gov. A copy of the answer must also be served on the OED Director by mail to Mail Stop 8, Office of the Solicitor, USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313‑1450.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish a Notice of Interim Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the practitioner's name, registration number, that the practitioner has been suspended on an interim basis pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.25(b), and the crimes adjudicated (with statutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample Notice text is included in the Order; it also advises that disciplinary decisions are available at the OED FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to government entities and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to (i) appropriate employees of the USPTO; (ii) interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States; and (iii) appropriate authorities of any state in which the practitioner is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures other relevant authorities and courts are informed of the practitioner's interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (obligations upon suspension or disbarment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not restate § 11.58, it expressly requires compliance, which typically includes client notification, transfer of files, and related responsibilities during suspension; the limited recognition period is granted only to permit compliance with § 11.58(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the practitioner's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This administrative action prevents access/use of USPTO electronic systems under those customer numbers while the practitioner is suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number while suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: The respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction preserves the effect of suspension with respect to electronic filing/access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review does not stay suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner seeks review of the suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeking appellate or other review does not stay the interim suspension; the suspension remains in effect during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catch‑all for additional relief
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order reserves authority to grant such other and further relief as the nature of the cause shall require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits the Director or adjudicator to impose additional measures necessary to protect the public interest or effectuate disciplinary objectives.
